data_schema.title: USDA Directive Extraction Schema v2.1 (DR/DM)
data_schema.description: Extracts metadata and structured policy statements from 3000 series USDA Departmental Regulation (DR) or Departmental Manual (DM). Governing rules: (1) Any field described as verbatim must be copied character-for-character from the source document. Never paraphrase, merge, abbreviate, summarize, or insert ellipses. (2) Do not infer. If the source does not support an optional field, leave the field out entirely. Never return an empty string or a guess. (3) Only the label fields in policy_statements (statement_kind, statement_function, modal_use, normative_force, actor_basis) are interpretations. Every other field is quoted or copied from the document.

document_type.description: Type of document as printed in the header, such as 'Departmental Regulation' or 'Departmental Manual'.

issuing_organization.description: Organization issuing the document, verbatim from the header.

issuing_location.description: Location of the issuing organization, verbatim from the header.

regulation_number.description: Official document number from the header, verbatim, for example 'DR 3105-001'.

subject.description: Subject or title of the document, verbatim from the header.

issue_date.description: Issue date from the header, as written.

expiration_date.description: Expiration date from the header, as written. Leave out if none is printed.

opi.description: Office of Primary Interest (OPI) from the header, verbatim.

supersedes.description: The prior document this document supersedes. Take all values from the supersession paragraph in the body (usually under Special Instructions/Cancellations), NOT from the header. Leave the whole object out if the document supersedes nothing.

document_number.description: Number of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph. If it is identical to this document's own number, still copy it from the supersession paragraph, not the header.

document_title.description: Title of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

document_date.description: Date of the superseded document as written in the supersession paragraph.

scope.description: The text of the Scope section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Scope section.

purpose.description: The text of the Purpose section, verbatim. Do not add words. Leave out if the document has no Purpose section.

inquiries.description: Contact information from the Inquiries section. Leave out any property the document does not state; never return an empty string.

office.description: Office or division named for inquiries, verbatim. Leave out if the document names no office.

email.description: Email address given for inquiries, verbatim, without trailing punctuation. Leave out if none is given.

table_of_contents.description: Top-level entries of the printed table of contents, in order, including appendices. Return an empty list if the document prints no table of contents.

section_number.description: Section or appendix identifier as printed, for example '1.' or 'Appendix A'.

section_title.description: Section or appendix title as printed in the table of contents.

page.description: Page number exactly as printed in the table of contents, for example '2' or 'A-1'. Copy it even if the section actually starts on a different page. Leave out if no page number is printed.

actors.description: Registry of every distinct entity that the policy text names in an acting role. One entry per entity. Include every entity used as actor_name in policy_statements. Also include entities the document names in a role without being directed to act (mark those mentioned_only). Documents (bylaws, regulations, directives) are NEVER actors and must not appear here. Return an empty list if the document names no actors.

name.description: The entity's name exactly as written in the policy text, without a leading article ('the') and without a possessive. Keep a compound name intact if the document writes it as one phrase, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'. This is the join key used by actor_name in policy_statements, so spell it identically there.

components.description: ONLY for a name that joins separate entities with commas or 'and' (for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices' gives 'USDA Mission Areas', 'agencies', 'staff offices'). NEVER split a job title from the organization that qualifies it ('Director of IT, Office of the Inspector General' is ONE position), and never split an organization name from the position it modifies ('Office of the Chief Information Officer (OCIO) Associate CIOs (ACIO)' is ONE group). Each component is a verbatim substring of the name. Leave out for single entities.

items.description: One verbatim component of a compound actor name.

actor_type.description: Kind of entity. Use exactly one of: position (a job title, singular or plural, for example 'USDA CIO' or 'Mission Area Assistant CIOs'), office (an organizational unit, for example 'OCIO Executive Secretariat'), council_or_body (a council, committee, board, or similar body), group (a category of organizations or units, not job titles, for example 'USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices'), external_entity (an entity outside the document's authority), program_or_system (an IT initiative, system, program, or project that the document says must act or conform).

binding_status.description: bound_by_this_document: the document directs, permits, or assigns a function or role to this entity and has authority over it. mentioned_only: the document names the entity but cannot or does not impose anything on it (for example a council or agency outside USDA that the document says a USDA body partners with).

policy_statements.description: Structured statements from the numbered body sections only (not the table of contents, not the appendices). RULES. (a) SENTENCES: emit one statement per sentence. If a paragraph has more than one sentence, give each its own statement with ids suffixed .s1, .s2, and so on. Abbreviations and legal citations ('U.S.C.', 'CFR', '§', 'et seq.') do not end a sentence. (b) LISTS: when text introduces a list (usually ends with a colon, for example 'The USDA CIO will:'), emit the introducing text as one statement with statement_kind 'lead_in', and emit EVERY item of the list as its own statement with statement_kind 'list_item' and parent_statement_id set to the id of the lead_in. Never skip list items, including lists of legal authorities. For a list inside a list, parent_statement_id is the immediate parent. (c) NEVER merge text from different sentences, paragraphs, or list items into one statement. (d) Copy text exactly; do not summarize. (e) PRONOUNS: when a sentence's subject is a pronoun ('It', 'Its', 'They') that refers to a named actor in the preceding sentence, resolve it: set actor_name to that actor and actor_basis to resolved_from_prior_sentence. (f) DOCUMENT AS SUBJECT: when the grammatical subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'), leave actor_name out; the entities the document acts on belong in target.

statement_id.description: Printed numbering path of the statement: section number, then paragraph letter, then item number in parentheses, for example '1', '3.a', '5.d.s2', '6.a(1)'. Add '.sN' only when a paragraph contains more than one sentence. Must be unique within the document.

statement_kind.description: standalone: a complete sentence that stands on its own. lead_in: text that introduces a list and is incomplete without its items. list_item: a list item that completes its lead_in.

parent_statement_id.description: Include ONLY when statement_kind is list_item: the statement_id of its immediate lead_in. For every other statement leave this field out entirely; never return an empty string.

section_number.description: Number of the section containing the statement, digits only, for example '6'.

section_title.description: Title of the section containing the statement, as shown in the table of contents, for example 'Roles and Responsibilities'.

source_text.description: VERBATIM text of this one sentence or list item exactly as printed, including trailing punctuation such as ':' or ';' and including any list-ending words such as 'and'. No paraphrase, no ellipses, no text from any other statement. For a list_item, give only the item's own text, not the lead_in.

statement_function.description: What the statement does. obligation: a required action or compliance requirement on an actor. responsibility: a standing duty or function assigned to an actor, including present-tense descriptions of what a body does. role_designation: assigns an entity to a role, for example membership or voting status. authority: names a legal source of authority or a grant of authority. scope: states what or whom the document applies to. purpose: states why the document or a body exists. definition: defines a term. condition: states a standalone triggering condition. exception: carves out an exception. savings_clause: states that the document does not displace existing authorities or delegations. effectivity: states when the document takes effect or how long it lasts. supersession: states that the document replaces another. classification_rule: states a rule that classifies something or applies a requirement when a status is met. reference: points to another document or location. inquiry: tells who may be contacted. container: use for every lead_in statement. other: none of the above.

modal_verb.description: The modal word or phrase of the statement's MAIN clause, exactly as written, for example 'will', 'can', 'may', 'must', 'shall', 'must not'. Ignore modals inside relative or subordinate clauses (for 'advises the USDA CIO on IT matters that may become IT investments', the 'may' is not the statement's modal). For a list_item whose own text has no modal, copy the modal from its lead_in. Leave out if the main clause has no modal.

modal_use.description: deontic: the main-clause modal directs, permits, or prohibits action by an actor (for example 'The Deputy CIO will serve', 'can direct questions'). predictive: the modal only states what will happen or remain true (for example 'It will remain in effect until superseded'). none: the main clause has no modal.

normative_force.description: mandatory: deontic 'will', 'shall', or 'must' directing an actor to act or to serve in a role. prohibitive: deontic 'must not', 'shall not', or 'may not'. permissive: deontic 'may' or 'can'. assigned: a present-tense statement with no deontic modal that assigns or describes a function, duty, or role of a named actor (for example 'The CIO Council advises the USDA CIO on...', 'It assesses the needs of...'); use it only when actor_name is present, and never for purpose statements. descriptive: everything else with no deontic force, including purpose, scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, references, authorities, definitions, and statements about the document itself or about other documents. not_applicable: use for every lead_in; its force is carried by its list_items.

actor_name.description: The entity directed to act, permitted to act, or assigned a function or role by this statement, spelled exactly as in the matching actors[].name. It must appear in source_text or in the lead_in's text (leading article removed); for a resolved pronoun, copy it from the antecedent sentence. Leave out when the statement binds no actor: scope, supersession, effectivity, savings clauses, statements about documents (including bylaws), and any statement whose subject is the document itself ('This DR', 'This policy', 'Nothing in this DR'). Never supply an actor that is not stated in the text or resolvable from the preceding sentence. Always leave out for lead_in statements.

actor_basis.description: Include ONLY when actor_name is present; otherwise leave this field out entirely. explicit_in_statement: the actor appears in this statement's own source_text. inherited_from_lead_in: the actor appears only in the lead_in that this list_item completes. resolved_from_prior_sentence: the subject is a pronoun resolved to the actor named in the preceding sentence.

target.description: VERBATIM phrase naming what the action is directed at or what the statement applies to, starting at the first word after any leading article ('a', 'an', 'the'). For a role_designation, the body or unit the role is within (for example 'CIO Council'). Leave out if none.

resulting_status.description: VERBATIM phrase naming the status or role that a role_designation or classification_rule confers, for example 'voting member' or 'advisory (non-voting) members'. Leave out for other statements.

conditions.description: VERBATIM phrases that restrict when or to what the statement applies, for example 'that the CIO Council designates as enterprise initiatives'. Do NOT treat a non-restrictive descriptive phrase set off by commas (for example 'appointed by the USDA CIO' in 'The Secretariat, appointed by the USDA CIO, will serve') as a condition. Leave out if there are none.

items.description: One verbatim condition phrase copied from source_text.

cross_references.description: Other documents, laws, or regulations cited in source_text, each copied verbatim as ONE entry per cited authority, including its code citation (for example 'The Clinger-Cohen Act of 1996, 40 United States Code (U.S.C.) § 11101 et seq.' is one entry; for a list_item that is just a citation, the entry is the item text without the trailing ';' or 'and'). Never add a separate entry for a title that is part of the same citation (the words 'Chief Information Officer' after '7 CFR § 2.32'). Never list generic categories such as 'law' or 'Federal regulation'. Leave out if none.

acronyms.description: Acronyms and abbreviations listed in the acronym appendix, one entry per row, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no acronym appendix.

acronym.description: Acronym or abbreviation exactly as printed.

authorities_and_references.description: Entries of the Authorities and References appendix, one per entry, each copied verbatim, including any date, in order. Return an empty list if the document has no such appendix.

items.description: One appendix entry exactly as printed, joined across line breaks.

policy_statements.source_text: This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the policy for the reporting and management of Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) activities and the acquisition and management of data acquired by UAS within the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA).
policy_statements.target: reporting and management of Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) activities and the acquisition and management of data acquired by UAS within the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA)

policy_statements.source_text: This DR defines the strategic direction necessary to ensure the safeguarding of privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties of the citizens of the United States and USDA personnel when using UASs.
policy_statements.target: safeguarding of privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties of the citizens of the United States and USDA personnel

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, programs, teams, organizations, appointees, and employees.
policy_statements.target: all USDA Mission Areas, agencies, staff offices, programs, teams, organizations, appointees, and employees

policy_statements.source_text: This includes contractors and grantees operating on behalf of USDA.
policy_statements.target: contractors and grantees operating on behalf of USDA

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to all USDA UAS investments throughout their entire life cycle, regardless of funding source, whether owned and operated by USDA or operated on behalf of USDA.
conditions: throughout their entire life cycle
regardless of funding source
whether owned and operated by USDA or operated on behalf of USDA

policy_statements.source_text: UAS investments or services beyond USDA operational control and conducted off of USDA owned lands by cooperating agencies and staff offices are excluded.
conditions: beyond USDA operational control and conducted off of USDA owned lands by cooperating agencies and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: This DR applies to all USDA Information Technology (IT) investments throughout their entire life cycle, regardless of funding source, whether owned and operated by USDA or operated on behalf of USDA.

policy_statements.source_text: This DR is to ensure smart management of UAS flown data to protect Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and civil rights of in accordance to the DR 3080-001, Records Management, and DR 3465-001, Enterprise Geospatial Data Management (EGDM).
policy_statements.target: Personally Identifiable Information (PII) and civil rights

policy_statements.source_text: This DR does not apply to investigative operations or operations entirely under cooperator, entity under contract with the USDA who works with the USDA for by directional benefits, operational control and does not apply to fire suppression activities or to law enforcement activities commonly related to USDA Forest Service.
policy_statements.target: investigative operations or operations entirely under cooperator, entity under contract with the USDA who works with the USDA for by directional benefits, operational control

policy_statements.source_text: This DR is effective as of the publication date of this document and will remain in effect until superseded.
conditions: until superseded

policy_statements.source_text: All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices must align their policies with this DR within 6 months of the published date.
conditions: within 6 months of the published date
policy_statements.actor_name: All USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: USDA will establish, maintain, and continuously update the UAS DR practices in accordance with legislative regulations and Office of Management and Budget (OMB) guidelines for all USDA IT major and non-major investments according to DR 3130-008, Definition of Major Information Technology Investments, and DR 3130-009, Non-Major Information Technology (IT) Investments.
cross_references: DR 3130-008, Definition of Major Information Technology Investments

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA follows the guidelines of what is a UAS as defined by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Modernization and Reform Act of 2012, Public Law (P.L.) No. 112-95.
policy_statements.target: guidelines of what is a UAS
cross_references: Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) Modernization and Reform Act of 2012, Public Law (P.L.) No. 112-95

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will not deviate from this definition as defined in this Act and/or future revisions of this Act.
policy_statements.target: this definition as defined in this Act and/or future revisions of this Act

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA will follow future guidelines put forth from the FAA once reviewed for fitness in the USDA environment.
policy_statements.target: future guidelines put forth from the FAA

policy_statements.source_text: This DR expands the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) definition of PII as found in Special Publication (SP) 800-122, Guide to Protecting the Confidentiality of Personally Identifiable Information (PII).
policy_statements.target: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) definition of PII
cross_references: Special Publication (SP) 800-122, Guide to Protecting the Confidentiality of Personally Identifiable Information (PII)

policy_statements.source_text: The NIST definition of PII is as follows:
This document uses a broad definition of PII to identify as many potential sources of PII as possible (e.g., databases, shared network drives, backup tapes, and contractor sites).
PII is —any information about an individual maintained by an agency [or Mission Area, or staff office], including:
Any information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual’s identity, such as name, Social Security number (SSN), date and place of birth, mother’s maiden name, or biometric records; and
Any other information that is linked or linkable to an individual, such as medical, educational, financial, and employment information.
Five examples of PII include, but are not limited to:
Name, such as full name, maiden name, mother’s maiden name, or alias;
Personal identification number, such as SSN, passport number, driver’s license number, taxpayer identification number, or financial account or credit card number;
Address information, such as street address or email address;

Personal characteristics, including photographic image (especially of face or other identifying characteristic), fingerprints, handwriting, or other biometric data (e.g., retina scan, voice signature, facial geometry); and

Information about an individual that is linked or linkable to one of the above (e.g., date of birth, place of birth, race, religion, weight, activities, geographical indicators, employment information, medical information, education information, financial information).
The NIST definition does include facial geometry and voice signature but is strongly written for the tabular database environment where as UAS captures remotely sensed and imagery data.
In order to protect the PII of U.S. citizens and USDA personnel, the USDA will broaden the NIST definition to include:
UAS that acquire imagery at a resolution that can be used to identify an individual’s identity or read license plates must follow USDA guidelines to protect PII.
conditions: that acquire imagery at a resolution that can be used to identify an individual’s identity or read license plates

policy_statements.source_text: Face blurring will be required if people who are not part of the acquisition team are imaged;
conditions: if people who are not part of the acquisition team are imaged

policy_statements.source_text: USDA will not fly UAS sensors that can be used to record conversations without a privacy determination;
policy_statements.target: UAS sensors that can be used to record conversations
conditions: without a privacy determination

policy_statements.source_text: USDA may fly UAS instruments that can be used to augment communications (this is a likely future application for wildland fire);
policy_statements.target: UAS instruments that can be used to augment communications

policy_statements.source_text: USDA will not fly UAS instruments that can observe through houses or roofs without a privacy determination by the Mission Area, agency, or staff office conducting the flight using a Privacy Threshold Analysis (PTA); and
policy_statements.target: UAS instruments that can observe through houses or roofs
conditions: without a privacy determination by the Mission Area, agency, or staff office conducting the flight using a Privacy Threshold Analysis (PTA)

policy_statements.source_text: If a Mission Area, agency, or staff office sources out the collection of UAS data to “any” outside collection source, then the outside source collector must follow all USDA PII policies and approval procedures.
policy_statements.target: all USDA PII policies and approval procedures
conditions: If a Mission Area, agency, or staff office sources out the collection of UAS data to “any” outside collection source

policy_statements.source_text: If it is determined that the data acquired during a UAS project does contain PII and a determination from the Mission Area, agency, or staff office’s PTA was justified from the Mission Area, agency, or staff office, the Mission Area, agency, or staff office will only retain the data encrypted in a secure system with eAuthentication and it will not be retained greater than 180 days unless retention of the information is determined to be necessary to an authorized mission of the retaining Mission Area, agency, or staff office, is maintained in a system of records covered by the Privacy Act, or is required to be retained for a longer period by any other applicable law or regulation.
conditions: If it is determined that the data acquired during a UAS project does contain PII and a determination from the Mission Area, agency, or staff office’s PTA was justified from the Mission Area, agency, or staff office

unless retention of the information is determined to be necessary to an authorized mission of the retaining Mission Area, agency, or staff office, is maintained in a system of records covered by the Privacy Act, or is required to be retained for a longer period by any other applicable law or regulation

policy_statements.source_text: UAS-collected information that is not maintained in a system of records covered by the Privacy Act of 1974 will not be disseminated outside of the Mission Area, agency, or staff office unless dissemination is required by law, or fulfills an authorized purpose and complies with Mission Area, agency, or staff office requirements.

unless dissemination is required by law, or fulfills an authorized purpose and complies with Mission Area, agency, or staff office requirements

policy_statements.source_text: Additionally, if the PTA requires a Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA), it must be performed and submitted to their Mission Area, agency, or staff office security offices in accordance with the Departmental Manual (DM) 3515-002, Privacy Impact Assessment.
policy_statements.target: their Mission Area, agency, or staff office security offices
conditions: if the PTA requires a Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA)

policy_statements.source_text: This will not apply to emergency response situations using UAS and will be reviewed on a case-by-case situation by the USDA Geospatial Program Manager.
All UAS projects need to be conducted in accordance with current White House, FAA, USDA and Mission Area, agency, and staff office policy.

To provide for effective accountability, each USDA Mission Area, agency, and staff office is responsible for collaborative oversight and tracking of UAS flight activities within their respective agency.
policy_statements.target: collaborative oversight and tracking of UAS flight activities within their respective agency
policy_statements.actor_name: each USDA Mission Area, agency, and staff office

policy_statements.source_text: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices employing UAS or UAS-collected information shall comply with Departmental direction and take appropriate steps to ensure effective oversight and accountability for their respective UAS programs.
conditions: employing UAS or UAS-collected information
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Accordingly, USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices shall ensure that:
Oversight procedures are implemented for UAS use, including audits or assessments, in compliance with Departmental policies and regulations.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Mission Area, agency, and staff office personnel and contractors comply with UAS program training requirements, rules of behavior, and procedures for reporting suspected cases of misuse or abuse of UAS technologies.
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Area, agency, and staff office personnel and contractors

policy_statements.source_text: Policies and procedures are implemented that provide meaningful oversight of individuals who have access to sensitive information (including any PII) collected using UAS consistent with applicable Federal laws, regulations, and policies, as well as Departmental policy guidance.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Any data-sharing agreements or policies, data use policies, and records management policies applicable to UAS conform to applicable laws, regulations, and policies.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Policies and procedures are implemented to authorize the use of UAS in response to a request for UAS assistance in support of Federal, State, local, tribal, or territorial government operations.
policy_statements.actor_name: USDA Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: Any authorized use, letter of authorization, or memorandum of understanding must include the requirements of this policy and appropriate safeguards to protect privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties.
policy_statements.target: requirements of this policy and appropriate safeguards to protect privacy, civil rights, and civil liberties

policy_statements.source_text: Policies and procedures are to be implemented to keep the public informed about the USDA UAS program and to provide transparency in regard to where USDA UAS are authorized to operate in the US National Air Space (NAS) while not revealing information that could reasonably be expected to compromise law enforcement or national security.
Keep the public informed about the USDA UAS program as well as changes that would significantly affect privacy, civil rights, or civil liberties.

Make available to the public, on an annual basis, a general summary of USDA UAS operations during the previous fiscal year, to include a brief description of types or categories of missions flown, and the number of times the Mission Area, agency, or staff office provided assistance to other agencies, or to State, local, tribal, or territorial governments.
Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices will implement a redress program if there are public inquiries into the reported UAS activities.
conditions: if there are public inquiries into the reported UAS activities
policy_statements.actor_name: Mission Areas, agencies, and staff offices

policy_statements.source_text: The USDA CIO will:
Provide executive accountability for Departmental PII pertaining to the use of all UASs and the data collected from this platform;
Provide executive governance oversight over UAS technology-enabled business processes, including all geospatial capital assets created, provisioned, and consumed across the Department; and
Delegate executive leadership for UAS technology, data, and information solutions to the Enterprise Geospatial Program Manager.
The USDA Geospatial Information Officer (GIO) will:
Have authority, responsibility, and accountability for USDA Departmental UAS data retention and disposal of data containing PII;
policy_statements.target: USDA Departmental UAS data retention and disposal of data containing PII

policy_statements.source_text: Be responsible for reviewing all waiver requests in association with this DR and determining next steps of waiver.
policy_statements.target: all waiver requests in association with this DR

policy_statements.source_text: Act as the primary UAS point of contact at the Department level; and
Be responsible for all inquiries into this DR.
The USDA Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) will:
Review and act upon Plan of Action and Milestones (POA&M); and
Report to the GIO any outstanding POA&Ms related to waivers of this DR on an annual basis.

This DR does not apply to investigative operations or operations entirely under cooperator, entity under contract with the USDA who works with the USDA for by directional benefits, operational control and does not apply to fire suppression activities or to law enforcement activities commonly related to USDA Forest Service.

c. This DR expands the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) definition of PII as found in Special Publication  (SP) 800-122 , *Guide to Protecting the Confidentiality of Personally Identifiable Information (PII)*.
National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) definition of PII
The  NIST definition of PII  is as follows:
This document uses a broad definition of PII to identify as many potential sources of PII as possible (e.g., databases, shared network drives, backup tapes, and contractor sites).
PII is —any information about an individual maintained by an agency [or Mission Area, or staff office], including:
Any information that can be used to distinguish or trace an individual’s identity, such as name, Social Security number (SSN), date and place of birth, mother’s maiden name, or biometric records; and
Any other information that is linked or linkable to an individual, such as medical, educational, financial, and employment information.
Five examples of PII include, but are not limited to:
Name, such as full name, maiden name, mother’s maiden name, or alias;
Personal identification number, such as SSN, passport number, driver’s license number, taxpayer identification number, or financial account or credit card number;
Address information, such as street address or email address;

Personal characteristics, including photographic image (especially of face or other identifying characteristic), fingerprints, handwriting, or other biometric data (e.g., retina scan, voice signature, facial geometry); and

Information about an individual that is linked or linkable to one of the above (e.g., date of birth, place of birth, race, religion, weight, activities, geographical indicators, employment information, medical information, education information, financial information).
The NIST definition does include facial geometry and voice signature but is strongly written for the tabular database environment where as UAS captures remotely sensed and imagery data.
In order to protect the PII of U.S. citizens and USDA personnel, the USDA will broaden the NIST definition to include:

a. This Departmental Regulation (DR) establishes the policy for the reporting and management of Unmanned Aerial Systems (UAS) activities and the acquisition and management of data acquired by UAS within the United States Department of Agriculture (USDA).

b. This DR applies to all USDA UAS investments throughout their entire life cycle, regardless of funding source, whether owned and operated by USDA or operated on behalf of USDA. UAS investments or services beyond USDA operational control and conducted off of USDA owned lands by cooperating agencies and staff offices are excluded.
